diff --git a/tests/sentry/utils/test_safe_extract_zip_security.py b/tests/sentry/utils/test_safe_extract_zip_security.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/sentry/utils/test_safe_extract_zip_security.py
@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import io
+import stat
+import warnings
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from sentry.utils.zip import safe_extract_zip
+
+
+def _archive(*members: tuple[str, bytes | str, int | None]) -> io.BytesIO:
+    stream = io.BytesIO()
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(stream, "w") as archive:
+        for name, contents, mode in members:
+            if mode is None:
+                with warnings.catch_warnings():
+                    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
+                    archive.writestr(name, contents)
+                continue
+            info = zipfile.ZipInfo(name)
+            info.create_system = 3
+            info.external_attr = (mode | stat.S_IFMT(mode)) << 16
+            archive.writestr(info, contents)
+    stream.seek(0)
+    return stream
+
+
+def test_safe_extract_zip_extracts_nested_regular_files(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    safe_extract_zip(
+        _archive(("nested/file.txt", b"payload", None), ("nested/", b"", None)),
+        str(tmp_path),
+    )
+
+    assert (tmp_path / "nested/file.txt").read_bytes() == b"payload"
+
+
+def test_safe_extract_zip_accepts_filename_and_open_zipfile(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    archive_path = tmp_path / "archive.zip"
+    archive_path.write_bytes(_archive(("file.txt", b"payload", None)).getvalue())
+
+    safe_extract_zip(str(archive_path), str(tmp_path / "from_filename"))
+    assert (tmp_path / "from_filename/file.txt").read_bytes() == b"payload"
+
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
+        safe_extract_zip(archive, str(tmp_path / "from_open_archive"))
+        assert archive.namelist() == ["file.txt"]
+    assert (tmp_path / "from_open_archive/file.txt").read_bytes() == b"payload"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "member_name",
+    [
+        "../escape.txt",
+        "nested/../../escape.txt",
+        "..\\escape.txt",
+        "nested\\..\\escape.txt",
+        "/absolute.txt",
+        "C:\\absolute.txt",
+    ],
+)
+def test_unsafe_member_rejects_archive_before_writing(
+    tmp_path: Path, member_name: str
+) -> None:
+    destination = tmp_path / "destination"
+    outside = tmp_path / "escape.txt"
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        safe_extract_zip(
+            _archive(("good.txt", b"must not remain", None), (member_name, b"escape", None)),
+            str(destination),
+        )
+
+    assert not (destination / "good.txt").exists()
+    assert not outside.exists()
+
+
+def test_symlink_member_is_rejected_without_creating_output(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    symlink_mode = stat.S_IFLNK | 0o777
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        safe_extract_zip(
+            _archive(("link", "target", symlink_mode)),
+            str(tmp_path / "destination"),
+        )
+
+    assert not (tmp_path / "destination").exists()
+
+
+def test_duplicate_member_target_is_rejected_atomically(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        safe_extract_zip(
+            _archive(("same.txt", b"first", None), ("same.txt", b"second", None)),
+            str(tmp_path / "destination"),
+        )
+
+    assert not (tmp_path / "destination").exists()
+
+
+def test_existing_destination_symlink_cannot_escape_root(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    destination = tmp_path / "destination"
+    outside = tmp_path / "outside"
+    destination.mkdir()
+    outside.mkdir()
+    (destination / "link").symlink_to(outside, target_is_directory=True)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        safe_extract_zip(
+            _archive(("link/payload.txt", b"must not escape", None)),
+            str(destination),
+        )
+
+    assert not (outside / "payload.txt").exists()

+
+import re as _re_sim901
+
+_SIM901_BOOL_RE = _re_sim901.compile(
+    r"^(\d+):(\d+) SIM\d+ Use '(?P<inner>.+)' instead of 'bool\((?P=inner)\)'$"
+)
+
+
+def _sim901_bool_warnings(ret):
+    """Return [(line, col, inner)] for any 'Use X instead of bool(X)' warning,
+    independent of the specific SIMxxx rule code chosen by the implementation.
+    The issue does not pin down a code, so any unique SIM code is acceptable.
+    """
+    out = []
+    for msg in ret:
+        m = _SIM901_BOOL_RE.match(msg)
+        if m:
+            out.append((int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), m.group("inner")))
+    return out
+

+defmodule Ecto.MultiReadTest do
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
+
+  import Ecto.Query
+
+  alias Ecto.Multi
+  alias Ecto.TestRepo
+
+  defp query(source) do
+    from row in source, select: row.id
+  end
+
+  defp call_multi(fun, args) do
+    assert function_exported?(Multi, fun, length(args)),
+           "expected Ecto.Multi.#{fun}/#{length(args)} to be part of the public API"
+
+    apply(Multi, fun, args)
+  end
+
+  setup do
+    Process.delete(:test_repo_all_results)
+    :ok
+  end
+
+  test "exposes read operations in the canonical operation list" do
+    rows = query("multi_read_rows")
+    multi = call_multi(:all, [Multi.new(), :rows, rows, [prefix: "tenant"]])
+    multi = call_multi(:one, [multi, :row, rows, [timeout: 321]])
+    multi = call_multi(:exists?, [multi, :present, rows, []])
+
+    assert Multi.to_list(multi) == [
+      {:rows, {:all, rows, [prefix: "tenant"]}},
+      {:row, {:one, rows, [timeout: 321]}},
+      {:present, {:exists?, rows, []}}
+    ]
+  end
+
+  test "all returns every row and preserves query options" do
+    Process.put(:test_repo_all_results, {2, [[11], [22]]})
+    rows = query("multi_read_all")
+    multi = call_multi(:all, [Multi.new(), :rows, rows, [prefix: "tenant"]])
+
+    assert {:ok, %{rows: [11, 22]}} = TestRepo.transaction(multi)
+    assert_received {:all, executed}
+    assert executed.prefix == "tenant"
+  end
+
+  test "one returns nil for no rows, the value for one row, and rejects many rows" do
+    rows = query("multi_read_one")
+
+    Process.put(:test_repo_all_results, {0, []})
+    empty = call_multi(:one, [Multi.new(), :row, rows, [prefix: "tenant_one"]])
+    assert {:ok, %{row: nil}} = TestRepo.transaction(empty)
+    assert_received {:all, %{prefix: "tenant_one"}}
+
+    Process.put(:test_repo_all_results, {1, [[42]]})
+    single = call_multi(:one, [Multi.new(), :row, rows, []])
+    assert {:ok, %{row: 42}} = TestRepo.transaction(single)
+
+    Process.put(:test_repo_all_results, {2, [[1], [2]]})
+    many = call_multi(:one, [Multi.new(), :row, rows, []])
+    assert_raise Ecto.MultipleResultsError, fn -> TestRepo.transaction(many) end
+  end

+    rows = query("multi_read_exists")
+
+    Process.put(:test_repo_all_results, {1, [[1]]})
+    present = call_multi(:exists?, [Multi.new(), :present, rows, [prefix: "tenant_exists"]])
+    assert {:ok, %{present: true}} = TestRepo.transaction(present)
+    assert_received {:all, present_query}
+    assert present_query.prefix == "tenant_exists"
+    assert inspect(present_query) =~ "limit: 1"
+    assert inspect(present_query) =~ "select: 1"
+
+    Process.put(:test_repo_all_results, {0, []})
+    absent = call_multi(:exists?, [Multi.new(), :present, rows, []])
+    assert {:ok, %{present: false}} = TestRepo.transaction(absent)

+    blocked = call_multi(:all, [blocked, :never, query("multi_read_blocked"), []])

+    refute_received {:all, %{from: %{source: {"multi_read_blocked", nil}}}}
+  end

+def test_append_mode_file_not_corrupted_empty_df(ext):
+
+    import os
+
+    df = DataFrame()
+    with tm.ensure_clean(ext) as f:
+        with ExcelWriter(f, mode="w", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+            df.to_excel(writer)
+        size_after_w = os.path.getsize(f)
+
+        with ExcelWriter(f, mode="a", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+            df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Sheet2")
+        size_after_a = os.path.getsize(f)
+
+
+
+
+        assert size_after_a < size_after_w * 1.5, (
+            f"File bloated after append: {size_after_w} -> {size_after_a}"
+        )
+
+
+def test_append_mode_file_size_matches_fresh_write(ext):
+
+
+    import os
+
+    df = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2, 3]})
+
+    with tm.ensure_clean(ext) as f_appended:
+        with ExcelWriter(f_appended, mode="w", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+            df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="S1")
+        with ExcelWriter(f_appended, mode="a", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+            df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="S2")
+        size_appended = os.path.getsize(f_appended)
+
+    with tm.ensure_clean(ext) as f_fresh:
+        with ExcelWriter(f_fresh, mode="w", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+            df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="S1")
+            df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="S2")
+        size_fresh = os.path.getsize(f_fresh)
+
+
+    assert size_appended < size_fresh * 1.2, (
+        f"Append-mode file larger than expected: fresh={size_fresh}, "
+        f"appended={size_appended}"
+    )
+
+
+def test_append_mode_repeated_appends_no_bloat(ext):
+
+    import os
+
+    df = DataFrame({"A": [1]})
+    with tm.ensure_clean(ext) as f:
+        with ExcelWriter(f, mode="w", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+            df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="S0")
+        size_initial = os.path.getsize(f)
+
+        for i in range(1, 4):
+            with ExcelWriter(f, mode="a", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+                df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name=f"S{i}")
+
+        size_final = os.path.getsize(f)
+
+
+        with tm.ensure_clean(ext) as f_fresh:
+            with ExcelWriter(f_fresh, mode="w", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+                for i in range(4):
+                    df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name=f"S{i}")
+            size_fresh = os.path.getsize(f_fresh)
+
+
+
+        assert size_final < size_fresh * 1.5, (
+            f"Repeated appends bloated file: fresh={size_fresh}, "
+            f"after_appends={size_final}"
+        )
+
+
+def test_append_mode_data_readable(ext):
+
+    df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2, 3]})
+    df2 = DataFrame({"B": [4, 5, 6]})
+

+            df1.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="S1", index=False)
+        with ExcelWriter(f, mode="a", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
+            df2.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="S2", index=False)

+

+import unittest
+
+from datasets import Dataset
+from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+from axolotl.utils.data.pretraining import wrap_pretraining_dataset
+from axolotl.utils.dict import DictDefault
+
+
+class TestPretrainingNoPacking(unittest.TestCase):
+
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("huggyllama/llama-7b")
+        cls.tokenizer.pad_token = "</s>"
+
+    def test_no_packing_iterates_without_value_error(self):
+
+        texts = [f"This is example text number {i} with some words to tokenize " * 4 for i in range(40)]
+        dataset = Dataset.from_dict({"text": texts})
+        cfg = DictDefault({"sample_packing": False})
+
+        wrapped = wrap_pretraining_dataset(
+            dataset,
+            self.tokenizer,
+            cfg,
+            ds_wrapper_fn=None,
+            max_tokens=64,
+            batch_size=1,
+            seed=42,
+            buffer_size=10_000,
+        )
+
+        samples = list(wrapped)
+        assert len(samples) > 0
+        for sample in samples:
+            assert "input_ids" in sample
+            assert "labels" in sample
+            assert "attention_mask" in sample
+
+    def test_no_packing_outputs_padded_to_max_tokens(self):
+
+        texts = ["hello world how are you today " * 3 for _ in range(30)]
+        dataset = Dataset.from_dict({"text": texts})
+        cfg = DictDefault({"sample_packing": False})
+
+        max_tokens = 48
+        wrapped = wrap_pretraining_dataset(
+            dataset,
+            self.tokenizer,
+            cfg,
+            ds_wrapper_fn=None,
+            max_tokens=max_tokens,
+            batch_size=1,
+            seed=42,
+        )
+
+        samples = list(wrapped)
+        assert len(samples) > 0
+        for sample in samples:
+            assert len(sample["input_ids"]) == max_tokens
+            assert len(sample["labels"]) == max_tokens
+            assert len(sample["attention_mask"]) == max_tokens
+
+    def test_no_packing_tokenizes_text_column_content(self):
+
+        marker = "uniquemarkertoken"
+        texts = [f"{marker} alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta " * 2 for _ in range(20)]
+        dataset = Dataset.from_dict({"text": texts})
+        cfg = DictDefault({"sample_packing": False})
+
+        wrapped = wrap_pretraining_dataset(
+            dataset,
+            self.tokenizer,
+            cfg,
+            ds_wrapper_fn=None,
+            max_tokens=64,
+            batch_size=1,
+            seed=42,
+        )
+
+        samples = list(wrapped)
+        assert len(samples) > 0
+        decoded_first = self.tokenizer.decode(samples[0]["input_ids"])
+        assert marker in decoded_first, (
+            f"Expected '{marker}' from text column in decoded output; got: {decoded_first!r}"
+        )
+
+    def test_no_packing_with_extra_columns_only_tokenizes_text(self):
+
+
+
+
+
+        text_marker = "thetextcolumncontent"
+        meta_marker = "themetadatacontent"
+        texts = [f"{text_marker} alpha beta gamma delta " * 3 for _ in range(20)]
+        metadata = [f"{meta_marker} something irrelevant " * 3 for _ in range(20)]
+        dataset = Dataset.from_dict({"text": texts, "metadata": metadata})
+        cfg = DictDefault({"sample_packing": False})
+
+        wrapped = wrap_pretraining_dataset(
+            dataset,
+            self.tokenizer,
+            cfg,
+            ds_wrapper_fn=None,
+            max_tokens=64,
+            batch_size=1,
+            seed=42,
+        )
+
+        samples = list(wrapped)
+        assert len(samples) > 0
+
+        all_decoded = " ".join(self.tokenizer.decode(s["input_ids"]) for s in samples)
+        assert text_marker in all_decoded
+        assert meta_marker not in all_decoded
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

#!/bin/bash
set -e
cd /testbed

# Install jq 1.6 (jq 1.7 removed --argfile which the tests need)
if ! jq --argfile /dev/null /dev/null -n 'true' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -sL -o /usr/local/bin/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.6/jq-linux64
    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jq
fi

# Fix vendored codec library incompatibility with Go 1.22+
# (duplicate character in base64 alphabet causes panic at init)
sed -i 's|ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789__|ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_|' vendor/github.com/ugorji/go/codec/gen.go

# Set up GOPATH structure for this older Go project
export GOPATH=/root/go

+import unittest
+
+from pycute import *
+

+class TestSwizzleComposedLayout(unittest.TestCase):
+  def _call(self, fn):
+    try:
+      return fn()
+    except Exception as exc:
+      self.fail(f"public layout operation raised {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
+
+  def test_swizzle_is_layout_and_has_extent(self):
+    swizzle = Swizzle(2, 1, 2)
+    self.assertTrue(is_layout(swizzle))
+    self.assertEqual(self._call(swizzle.size), 32)
+    self.assertEqual(self._call(swizzle.cosize), 32)
+
+  def test_swizzle_mapping_is_bijective_for_both_shift_directions(self):
+    for swizzle in (Swizzle(2, 1, 2), Swizzle(2, 0, -3)):
+      extent = 32
+      values = [swizzle(i) for i in range(extent)]
+      self.assertEqual(sorted(values), list(range(extent)))
+      self.assertEqual([swizzle(value) for value in values], list(range(extent)))
+
+  def test_zero_bit_swizzle_is_identity(self):
+    swizzle = Swizzle(0, 3, 0)
+    self.assertEqual(self._call(swizzle.size), 8)
+    self.assertEqual(self._call(swizzle.cosize), 8)
+    self.assertEqual([swizzle(i) for i in range(8)], list(range(8)))
+
+  def test_swizzle_value_equality_is_structural(self):
+    self.assertEqual(Swizzle(2, 1, 2), Swizzle(2, 1, 2))
+    self.assertNotEqual(Swizzle(2, 1, 2), Swizzle(1, 1, 2))
+    self.assertNotEqual(Swizzle(2, 1, 2), Swizzle(2, 0, -2))
+    self.assertFalse(Swizzle(2, 1, 2) == Layout(32))
+
+  def _composed(self):
+    return ComposedLayout(Layout(64, 3), 5, Layout((2, 3), (1, 2)))
+
+  def test_composed_mapping_and_extents(self):
+    composed = self._composed()
+    self.assertTrue(is_layout(composed))
+    self.assertEqual(composed(1, 2), 30)
+    self.assertEqual(size(composed), 6)
+    self.assertEqual(cosize(composed), 190)
+
+  def test_composed_mode_indexing_preserves_mapping(self):
+    composed = self._composed()
+    self.assertEqual(composed[0](1), composed(1, 0))
+    self.assertEqual(composed[1](2), composed(0, 2))
+
+  def test_composed_value_equality_is_type_safe(self):
+    composed = self._composed()
+    self.assertEqual(composed, self._composed())
+    self.assertNotEqual(composed, ComposedLayout(Layout(64, 3), 6, Layout((2, 3), (1, 2))))

+import asyncio
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from pyrogram import Client, raw
+from pyrogram.session import Session
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+API_ID = 12345
+API_HASH = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
+
+
+class RecordingSession:
+    active_sessions = 0
+    max_active_sessions = 0
+
+    def __init__(self, response=None, error=None):
+        self.calls = []
+        self.response = response or SimpleNamespace(label="raw-state", users=[], chats=[])
+        self.error = error
+        self.closed = False
+        RecordingSession.active_sessions += 1
+        RecordingSession.max_active_sessions = max(
+            RecordingSession.max_active_sessions,
+            RecordingSession.active_sessions,
+        )
+
+    async def invoke(self, query, retries, timeout, sleep_threshold):
+        self.calls.append((query, retries, timeout, sleep_threshold))
+        if self.error:
+            raise self.error
+        return self.response
+
+    async def stop(self):
+        if not self.closed:
+            self.closed = True
+            RecordingSession.active_sessions -= 1
+
+
+def run(coro):
+    return asyncio.run(coro)
+
+
+async def make_started_client(name="invoke-session", **kwargs):
+    app = Client(
+        name,
+        api_id=API_ID,
+        api_hash=API_HASH,
+        in_memory=True,
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+    await app.storage.open()
+    app.is_connected = True
+    app.is_initialized = False
+    app.session = RecordingSession()
+    return app
+
+
+async def close_started_client(app):
+    if app.is_connected:
+        await app.disconnect()
+
+
+def test_invoke_before_start_raises_specific_connection_error():
+
+
+
+
+
+    async def scenario():
+        app = Client("not-started", api_id=API_ID, api_hash=API_HASH, in_memory=True)
+
+        assert not app.is_connected
+
+        with pytest.raises(ConnectionError) as raised:
+            await app.invoke(raw.functions.updates.GetState())
+
+        assert str(raised.value) == "Client has not been started yet"
+
+    run(scenario())
+
+
+def test_started_invoke_returns_raw_response_and_forwards_default_threshold():
+
+
+
+
+
+    async def scenario():
+        app = await make_started_client(sleep_threshold=33)
+        try:
+            query = raw.functions.updates.GetState()
+
+            result = await app.invoke(query, retries=3, timeout=4.5)
+            sent_query, retries, timeout, sleep_threshold = app.session.calls[0]
+
+
+            assert result is app.session.response
+            assert len(app.session.calls) == 1
+
+            assert sent_query is query
+            assert retries == 3
+            assert timeout == 4.5
+            assert sleep_threshold == 33
+        finally:
+            await close_started_client(app)
+
+    run(scenario())
+
+

+
+
+
+
+

+
+def assert_frame_equal_missing(left, right):
+
+    left = left.astype(object).where(left.notna(), pd.NA)
+    right = right.astype(object).where(right.notna(), pd.NA)
+    assert_frame_equal(left, right, check_dtype=False)
+
+
+def test_separate_extra_drop_preserves_position_and_index():
+    data = pd.DataFrame(
+        {"id": [2, 1], "label": ["a-b-c", "d-e-f"], "tail": ["x", "y"]},
+        index=[10, 20],
+    )
+    dropped = separate(data, "label", ["first", "rest"], sep="-", extra="drop")
+    expected = pd.DataFrame(
+        {"id": [2, 1], "first": ["a", "d"], "rest": ["b", "e"], "tail": ["x", "y"]},
+        index=[10, 20],
+    )
+    assert_frame_equal(dropped, expected)
+
+
+def test_separate_extra_merge_joins_remaining_pieces():
+    data = pd.DataFrame(
+        {"id": [2, 1], "label": ["a-b-c", "d-e-f"], "tail": ["x", "y"]},
+        index=[10, 20],
+    )
+    merged = separate(data, _.label, ["first", "rest"], sep="-", extra="merge")
+    expected = pd.DataFrame(
+        {"id": [2, 1], "first": ["a", "d"], "rest": ["b-c", "e-f"], "tail": ["x", "y"]},
+        index=[10, 20],
+    )

+
+

+    data = pd.DataFrame({"label": ["a-b-c", "d"]})

+        out = separate(data, "label", ["x", "y"], sep="-", extra="warn")
+    assert_frame_equal_missing(out, pd.DataFrame({"x": ["a", "d"], "y": ["b", None]}))
+
+    with pytest.warns(UserWarning):
+        padded = separate(pd.DataFrame({"label": ["a"]}), "label", ["x", "y"])
+    assert_frame_equal_missing(padded, pd.DataFrame({"x": ["a"], "y": [None]}))
+
+
+def test_separate_fill_right_aligns_missing_pieces():
+    data = pd.DataFrame({"label": ["a-b", "c"]})
+    right = separate(data, "label", ["x", "y", "z"], sep="-", fill="right")
+    assert_frame_equal_missing(
+        right,
+        pd.DataFrame({"x": ["a", "c"], "y": ["b", None], "z": [None, None]}),
+    )
+
+
+def test_separate_fill_left_aligns_missing_pieces():
+    data = pd.DataFrame({"label": ["a-b", "c"]})
+    left = separate(data, "label", ["x", "y", "z"], sep="-", fill="left")
+    assert_frame_equal_missing(

+        pd.DataFrame({"x": [None, None], "y": ["a", None], "z": ["b", "c"]}),

+            "episode": [2, 4],
+            "suffix": ["u", "v"],
+        }
+    )

+    data = pd.DataFrame({"label": ["a-b"]})
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):

+using Test
+using Random
+using LazySets
+
+mutable struct CyclingVectorSource{N}
+    values::Vector{Vector{N}}
+    index::Int
+end
+
+function Base.rand(rng::AbstractRNG, d::CyclingVectorSource, n::Int)
+    x = d.values[d.index]
+    d.index = d.index == length(d.values) ? 1 : d.index + 1
+    @test length(x) == n
+    return copy(x)
+end
+
+function _on_set(x, S)
+    return isapproxzero(dot(S.a, x) - S.b)
+end
+
+@testset "project point to Hyperplane" begin
+    H = Hyperplane([2.0, 1.0, -2.0], 3.0)
+
+    y = project([1.0, 2.0, 0.0], H)
+    @test y ≈ [7 / 9, 17 / 9, 2 / 9]
+    @test _on_set(y, H)
+    @test length(y) == dim(H)
+
+    member = [1.0, 1.0, 0.0]
+    @test project(member, H) ≈ member
+end
+
+@testset "project point to Line2D" begin
+    L = Line2D([2.0, 1.0], 3.0)
+
+    y = project([0.0, 0.0], L)
+    @test y ≈ [6 / 5, 3 / 5]
+    @test _on_set(y, L)
+    @test length(y) == dim(L)
+
+    member = [1.0, 1.0]
+    @test project(member, L) ≈ member
+end
+
+@testset "explicit HyperplaneSampler" begin
+    H = Hyperplane([2.0, -1.0, 1.0], 1.0)
+    xs = sample(H, 8; sampler=LazySets.HyperplaneSampler())
+    @test length(xs) == 8
+    for x in xs
+        @test length(x) == dim(H)
+        @test _on_set(x, H)
+    end
+
+    L = Line2D([2.0, 1.0], 3.0)
+    ys = sample(L, 8; sampler=LazySets.HyperplaneSampler())
+    @test length(ys) == 8
+    for y in ys
+        @test length(y) == dim(L)
+        @test _on_set(y, L)
+    end
+end
+
+@testset "default sample from hyperplane-like sets" begin
+    H = Hyperplane([1.0, 2.0, -1.0], 2.0)
+    xs = sample(H, 7)
+    @test length(xs) == 7
+    for x in xs
+        @test length(x) == dim(H)
+        @test _on_set(x, H)
+    end
+
+    L = Line2D([3.0, -1.0], 2.0)
+    ys = sample(L, 7)
+    @test length(ys) == 7
+    for y in ys
+        @test length(y) == dim(L)
+        @test _on_set(y, L)
+    end
+end
+
+@testset "HyperplaneSampler default and custom source" begin
+    H = Hyperplane([2.0, -1.0, 1.0], 1.0)
+
+    default_samples = sample(H, 3; sampler=LazySets.HyperplaneSampler())
+    @test length(default_samples) == 3
+    for x in default_samples
+        @test length(x) == dim(H)
+        @test _on_set(x, H)
+    end
+
+    L = Line2D([1.0, 1.0], 1.0)
+    source = CyclingVectorSource([[3.0, 0.0], [0.0, 4.0]], 1)

+    @test ys[2] ≈ [-1.5, 2.5]
+    for y in ys
+        @test _on_set(y, L)
+    end
+end

     mod = RollingOLS(y, x, 150, min_nobs=min_nobs)
     res = mod.fit()
     assert np.all(res.nobs[res.nobs != 0] >= min_nobs)
+
+
+def _gen_simple(nobs=120, nvar=3, seed=12345):
+    rs = np.random.RandomState(seed)
+    x = rs.standard_normal((nobs, nvar))
+    x = tools.add_constant(x)
+    beta = np.array([1.0, -0.5, 0.7, 0.3])
+    y = x @ beta + rs.standard_normal(nobs) * 0.5
+    return y, x
+
+
+def test_expanding_default_is_false():
+
+    y, x = _gen_simple(nobs=120, nvar=3)
+    window = 60
+    min_nobs = 12
+    mod = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs)
+    res = mod.fit()
+    params = np.asarray(res.params)
+
+
+    assert np.all(np.isnan(params[:window - 1]))
+    assert not np.any(np.isnan(params[window - 1:]))
+
+
+def test_expanding_true_fills_pre_window_indices():
+
+
+    y, x = _gen_simple(nobs=120, nvar=3)
+    window = 60
+    min_nobs = 12
+    mod = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs,
+                     expanding=True)
+    res = mod.fit()
+    params = np.asarray(res.params)
+
+    assert np.all(np.isnan(params[:min_nobs - 1]))
+
+
+    assert not np.any(np.isnan(params[min_nobs - 1:window - 1]))
+
+    assert not np.any(np.isnan(params[window - 1:]))
+
+
+def test_expanding_matches_ols_at_min_nobs():
+
+
+    from statsmodels.regression.linear_model import OLS
+    y, x = _gen_simple(nobs=120, nvar=3)
+    window = 60
+    min_nobs = 10
+    mod = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs,
+                     expanding=True)
+    res = mod.fit()
+    params = np.asarray(res.params)
+    expected = OLS(y[:min_nobs], x[:min_nobs]).fit().params
+    assert_allclose(params[min_nobs - 1], expected)
+
+
+def test_expanding_matches_ols_within_expanding_phase():
+
+
+    from statsmodels.regression.linear_model import OLS
+    y, x = _gen_simple(nobs=120, nvar=3)
+    window = 50
+    min_nobs = 8
+    mod = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs,
+                     expanding=True)
+    res = mod.fit()
+    params = np.asarray(res.params)
+
+    for i in (min_nobs - 1, min_nobs + 5, window // 2, window - 2):
+        expected = OLS(y[:i + 1], x[:i + 1]).fit().params
+        assert_allclose(params[i], expected,
+                        err_msg='mismatch at i={}'.format(i))
+
+
+def test_expanding_post_window_matches_rolling():
+
+
+    y, x = _gen_simple(nobs=120, nvar=3)
+    window = 40
+    min_nobs = 8
+    res_roll = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs).fit()
+    res_exp = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs,
+                         expanding=True).fit()
+    params_roll = np.asarray(res_roll.params)
+    params_exp = np.asarray(res_exp.params)
+    assert_allclose(params_exp[window - 1:], params_roll[window - 1:])
+
+
+def test_expanding_at_window_boundary_matches_rolling_first():
+
+
+    from statsmodels.regression.linear_model import OLS
+    y, x = _gen_simple(nobs=120, nvar=3)
+    window = 30
+    min_nobs = 5
+    res_exp = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs,
+                         expanding=True).fit()
+    params_exp = np.asarray(res_exp.params)
+    expected = OLS(y[:window], x[:window]).fit().params
+    assert_allclose(params_exp[window - 1], expected)
+
+
+def test_expanding_nobs_grows():
+
+
+    y, x = _gen_simple(nobs=100, nvar=3)
+    window = 30
+    min_nobs = 6
+    mod = RollingOLS(y, x, window=window, min_nobs=min_nobs,
+                     expanding=True)
+    res = mod.fit()
+    nobs_arr = np.asarray(res.nobs)
+
+    for i in range(min_nobs - 1, window - 1):
+        assert nobs_arr[i] == i + 1, \
+            'nobs at i={} expected {} got {}'.format(i, i + 1, nobs_arr[i])
+
+    for i in range(window - 1, len(y)):
+        assert nobs_arr[i] == window

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -u
export LANG=C LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

BIN="$TMP/rgb_fifo_harness"
( cd /workspace/repo || exit 1
    EXTRA_OBJS=()

    while IFS= read -r src; do
        case "$src" in
            src/daemon/command.c|src/daemon/led.c) continue ;;
        esac
        obj="$TMP/$(basename "$src" .c).o"
        cc -std=c11 -O2 -DNDEBUG -I/workspace/repo -I/workspace/repo/usercase-test-coderl/fixtures -pthread -c "$src" -o "$obj" || exit 1
        EXTRA_OBJS+=("$obj")
    done < <({ git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR HEAD -- 'src/daemon/*.c'; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard 'src/daemon/*.c'; } | sort -u)
    if ((${#EXTRA_OBJS[@]})); then
        ar rcs "$TMP/libdaemon_extra.a" "${EXTRA_OBJS[@]}" || exit 1
        EXTRA_LIB="$TMP/libdaemon_extra.a"
    else
        EXTRA_LIB=
    fi
    cc -std=c11 -O2 -DNDEBUG \
        -I/workspace/repo \
        -I/workspace/repo/usercase-test-coderl/fixtures \
        -pthread \
        /workspace/repo/usercase-test-coderl/fixtures/rgb_fifo_harness.c \
        /workspace/repo/src/daemon/command.c \
        /workspace/repo/src/daemon/led.c \
        ${EXTRA_LIB:+"$EXTRA_LIB"} \
        -o "$BIN" ) || { echo "FAIL: build" >&2; exit 1; }

cd "$TMP" || exit 1

field() {
    local line="$1" key="$2"
    printf '%s\n' "$line" | tr ' ' '\n' | awk -F= -v key="$key" '$1 == key { print $2; exit }'
}

mode_line() {
    local label="$1"
    grep "^$label " out || fail "missing $label line: $(cat out)"
}

assert_header() {
    local label="$1" expected_mode="$2" line
    line=$(sed -n '1p' out)

    [ "$(field "$line" readcmd)" = "0" ] || fail "$label readcmd: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" active)" = "1" ] || fail "$label active state: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" currentmode)" = "$expected_mode" ] || fail "$label current mode: $line"
}

assert_uniform_mode() {
    local label="$1" mode="$2" color="$3" line total expected_nonzero expected_sum r g b
    line=$(mode_line "$mode")
    total=$(field "$line" total)
    r=$((16#${color:0:2}))
    g=$((16#${color:2:2}))
    b=$((16#${color:4:2}))
    if [ "$color" = "000000" ]; then
        expected_nonzero=0
    else
        expected_nonzero=$total
    fi
    expected_sum=$((total * (r + g + b)))


    [ "$(field "$line" first)" = "$color" ] || fail "$label $mode first LED: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" middle)" = "$color" ] || fail "$label $mode middle LED: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" last)" = "$color" ] || fail "$label $mode last LED: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" rmin)" = "${color:0:2}" ] && [ "$(field "$line" rmax)" = "${color:0:2}" ] || fail "$label $mode red range: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" gmin)" = "${color:2:2}" ] && [ "$(field "$line" gmax)" = "${color:2:2}" ] || fail "$label $mode green range: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" bmin)" = "${color:4:2}" ] && [ "$(field "$line" bmax)" = "${color:4:2}" ] || fail "$label $mode blue range: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" nonzero)" = "$expected_nonzero" ] || fail "$label $mode nonzero count: $line"
    [ "$(field "$line" sum)" = "$expected_sum" ] || fail "$label $mode channel sum: $line"
}

+import { FilterType, isNegatedFilter, resolveNegatedFilter } from '../../../../shared/src/search/interactive/util'

+
+describe('interactive filter normalization', () => {
+    test('classifies filter names case-insensitively', () => {
+        expect(isSingularFilter('CASE')).toBe(true)
+        expect(isSingularFilter('Case')).toBe(true)
+        expect(isFiniteFilter('ARCHIVED' as FilterType)).toBe(true)
+        expect(isTextFilter('RePo' as FilterType)).toBe(true)
+    })
+
+    test('canonicalizes filter types and preserves aliases and negation', () => {
+        const result = convertPlainTextToInteractiveQuery('needle RePo:^acme/one$ CASE:no -F:^generated/')
+        expect(result.navbarQuery).toBe('needle')
+        expect(result.filtersInQuery).toEqual(
+            expect.objectContaining({
+                case: {
+                    type: FilterType.case,
+                    value: 'no',
+                    editable: false,
+                    negated: false,
+                },
+            })
+        )
+
+        const filters = Object.values(result.filtersInQuery)
+        expect(filters).toEqual(
+            expect.arrayContaining([
+                {
+                    type: FilterType.repo,
+                    value: '^acme/one$',
+                    editable: false,
+                    negated: false,
+                },
+                {
+                    type: FilterType.file,
+                    value: '^generated/',
+                    editable: false,
+                    negated: true,
+                },
+            ])
+        )
+
+        const repeated = convertPlainTextToInteractiveQuery('repo:one r:two')
+        expect(Object.values(repeated.filtersInQuery)).toEqual(
+            expect.arrayContaining([
+                expect.objectContaining({ type: FilterType.repo, value: 'one' }),
+                expect.objectContaining({ type: FilterType.repo, value: 'two' }),
+            ])

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import contextlib

+import os
+import random
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+REPO_ROOT = "/workspace/repo"
+if REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)
+
+from data import create_dataset
+from options.test_options import TestOptions
+from options.train_options import TrainOptions
+
+
+def parse_options(kind, args):
+    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
+        if kind == "train":
+            return TrainOptions(" ".join(args)).parse()
+        if kind == "test":
+            opt = TestOptions(" ".join(args)).parse()
+
+            opt.num_threads = 0
+            opt.batch_size = 1
+            opt.serial_batches = True
+            opt.no_flip = True
+            opt.display_id = -1
+            return opt
+    raise SystemExit("usage: probe_unaligned.py <pairs|tensor|epoch> <train|test> ... -- <options>")
+
+
+def make_loader(kind, args):
+    opt = parse_options(kind, args)
+    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
+        loader = create_dataset(opt)
+    return opt, loader
+
+
+def rel(root, path):
+    return os.path.relpath(path, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
+
+
+def fmt(values):
+    return ",".join(f"{float(value):.6f}" for value in values)
+
+
+def summarize_item(dataset, dataroot, index):
+    item = dataset[index]
+    a = item["A"]
+    b = item["B"]
+    print(f"item{index}.A_path={rel(dataroot, item['A_paths'])}")
+    print(f"item{index}.B_path={rel(dataroot, item['B_paths'])}")
+    print(f"item{index}.A_shape={'x'.join(map(str, a.shape))}")
+    print(f"item{index}.B_shape={'x'.join(map(str, b.shape))}")
+    print(f"item{index}.A_first={fmt(a[:, 0, 0])}")
+    print(f"item{index}.B_first={fmt(b[:, 0, 0])}")
+    print(f"item{index}.A_mean={fmt(a.mean(dim=(1, 2)))}")
+    print(f"item{index}.B_mean={fmt(b.mean(dim=(1, 2)))}")
+    print(f"item{index}.A_red_row0={fmt(a[0, 0, :])}")
+
+
+def main():
+    if "--" not in sys.argv:
+        raise SystemExit("missing -- before tool options")
+
+    command = sys.argv[1]
+    kind = sys.argv[2]
+    sep = sys.argv.index("--")
+    probe_args = sys.argv[3:sep]
+    tool_args = sys.argv[sep + 1 :]
+    dataroot = tool_args[tool_args.index("--dataroot") + 1]
+
+    seed = int(os.environ.get("PROBE_SEED", "0"))
+    random.seed(seed)
+    np.random.seed(seed)
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+
+    _, loader = make_loader(kind, tool_args)
+    dataset = loader.dataset
+
+    if command == "pairs":
+        print(f"len={len(dataset)}")
+
+        for index in map(int, probe_args):
+            item = dataset[index]
+            print(f"pair{index}={rel(dataroot, item['A_paths'])}|{rel(dataroot, item['B_paths'])}")
+        return
+
+    if command == "tensor":
+        summarize_item(dataset, dataroot, int(probe_args[0]))
+        return
+
+    if command == "flip":
+        index = int(probe_args[0])
+        saw_unflipped = False
+        saw_flipped = False
+        first_item = None
+        for seed in map(int, probe_args[1:]):
+            random.seed(seed)
+            np.random.seed(seed)
+            torch.manual_seed(seed)
+            item = dataset[index]
+            if first_item is None:
+                first_item = item
+            row = fmt(item["A"][0, 0, :])
+            saw_unflipped = saw_unflipped or row == "-1.000000,-0.498039,0.003922,1.000000"
+            saw_flipped = saw_flipped or row == "1.000000,0.003922,-0.498039,-1.000000"
+
+        print(f"item{index}.A_path={rel(dataroot, first_item['A_paths'])}")
+        print(f"item{index}.B_path={rel(dataroot, first_item['B_paths'])}")
+        print(f"item{index}.A_shape={'x'.join(map(str, first_item['A'].shape))}")
+        print(f"item{index}.saw_unflipped={str(saw_unflipped).lower()}")
+        print(f"item{index}.saw_flipped={str(saw_flipped).lower()}")
+        return
+
+    if command == "epoch":
+        index = int(probe_args[0])
+        for epoch in map(int, probe_args[1:]):
+            dataset.current_epoch = epoch
+            random.seed(seed)
+            np.random.seed(seed)
+            torch.manual_seed(seed)
+            item = dataset[index]
+            a = item["A"]
+            print(f"epoch{epoch}.A_shape={'x'.join(map(str, a.shape))}")
+        return
+
+    raise SystemExit(f"unknown command: {command}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+def test_psd_welch_median_bias_correction():
+    """Median average should divide by Allen-2012 bias factor.
+
+    Verifies that ``psd_array_welch(..., average='median')`` returns the
+    median of the unaggregated periodograms divided by the median bias
+    correction factor (Appendix B of Allen et al. 2012, also used by
+    SciPy's welch).
+    """
+    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
+    sfreq = 1000.
+    n_per_seg = 128
+    n_overlap = 0
+
+    n_times = n_per_seg * 8
+    x = rng.randn(2, n_times)
+
+    psd_med, _ = psd_array_welch(
+        x, sfreq, n_fft=n_per_seg, n_per_seg=n_per_seg,
+        n_overlap=n_overlap, average='median')
+    psd_unagg, _ = psd_array_welch(
+        x, sfreq, n_fft=n_per_seg, n_per_seg=n_per_seg,
+        n_overlap=n_overlap, average=None)
+
+    n_segments = psd_unagg.shape[-1]
+    assert n_segments == 8
+    bias = _expected_median_bias(n_segments)
+
+    assert not np.isclose(bias, 1.0)
+    expected = np.median(psd_unagg, axis=-1) / bias
+    assert_allclose(psd_med, expected)
+
+    assert not np.allclose(psd_med, np.median(psd_unagg, axis=-1))
+
+
+def test_psd_welch_median_bias_value():
+    """Median PSD must be scaled down by the exact bias factor.
+
+    Pins the numerical value of the bias for 8 segments, ensuring
+    candidates that compute a different bias (or skip the correction)
+    are rejected.
+    """
+    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
+    sfreq = 1000.
+    n_per_seg = 64
+
+    n_times = n_per_seg * 8
+    x = rng.randn(1, n_times)
+
+    psd_med, _ = psd_array_welch(
+        x, sfreq, n_fft=n_per_seg, n_per_seg=n_per_seg,
+        n_overlap=0, average='median')
+    psd_unagg, _ = psd_array_welch(
+        x, sfreq, n_fft=n_per_seg, n_per_seg=n_per_seg,
+        n_overlap=0, average=None)
+

+    assert n == 8

+
+
+class PassthroughColumn(Column):
+
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__("value", required=False)
+
+    def prepare_string(self, value):
+        return value
+
+
+class ColumnSerializationContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_json_preserves_scalar_types_at_every_nesting_level(self):
+        value = {
+            "count": 3,
+            "enabled": False,
+            "nested": [{"ratio": 1.5, "missing": None}],
+        }
+        encoded = JSONColumn("metadata", required=False).prepare_string(value)
+
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(encoded), value)
+        self.assertIsInstance(json.loads(encoded)["count"], int)
+        self.assertIs(json.loads(encoded)["enabled"], False)
+
+    def test_json_sanitizes_string_leaves_without_touching_scalars(self):
+        value = {"outer": ["  hello\tworld  ", {"n": 7, "flag": True}]}
+        encoded = JSONColumn("metadata", required=False).prepare_string(value)
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            json.loads(encoded),
+            {"outer": ["hello world", {"n": 7, "flag": True}]},
+        )
+
+    def test_json_uses_null_for_absent_or_empty_containers(self):
+        column = JSONColumn("metadata", required=False)
+        self.assertIsNone(column.prepare_string(None))
+        self.assertIsNone(column.prepare_string({}))
+        self.assertIsNone(column.prepare_string([]))
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(column.prepare_string([None])), [None])
+
+    def test_array_uses_postgres_literal_escaping(self):
+        column = ArrayColumn("values", required=False, base_column=PassthroughColumn())
+        value = ["simple", "has,comma", 'has"quote', r"has\slash", "NULL"]
+
+        encoded = column.prepare_string(value)
+        self.assertTrue(encoded.startswith("{") and encoded.endswith("}"))
+        self.assertIn('"has,comma"', encoded)
+        self.assertIn('"has\\\"quote"', encoded)
+        self.assertIn('"has\\\\slash"', encoded)

@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+import unittest
+
+import tatsu
+from tatsu.codegen import codegen
+from tatsu.exceptions import FailedParse
+
+
+LITERAL_TRUE = '''
+    @@ignorecase :: True
+    start = "AbC" $;
+'''
+
+LITERAL_FALSE = '''
+    @@ignorecase :: False
+    start = "AbC" $;
+'''
+
+KEYWORD_GRAMMAR = r'''
+    @@ignorecase :: True
+    @@keyword :: if ELSE
+    start = {id}+ $;
+    @name
+    id = /\w+/;
+'''
+
+PATTERN_GRAMMAR = r'''
+    @@ignorecase :: True
+    start = word $;
+    word = /[a-z]+/;
+'''
+
+
+class IgnorecaseContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_model_directive_and_parse_override(self):
+        model = tatsu.compile(LITERAL_TRUE, 'CaseModel')
+        self.assertEqual('AbC', model.parse('abc'))
+        self.assertEqual('AbC', model.parse('ABC'))
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            model.parse('ABC', ignorecase=False)
+        self.assertEqual('AbC', model.parse('ABC'))
+
+        strict = tatsu.compile(LITERAL_FALSE, 'StrictModel')
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            strict.parse('abc')
+        self.assertEqual('AbC', strict.parse('abc', ignorecase=True))
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            strict.parse('ABC', ignorecase=False)
+
+    def test_pattern_matching_remains_case_sensitive(self):
+        model = tatsu.compile(PATTERN_GRAMMAR, 'PatternModel')
+        self.assertEqual('abc', model.parse('abc'))
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            model.parse('ABC')
+
+    def test_keywords_follow_effective_case_mode(self):
+        model = tatsu.compile(KEYWORD_GRAMMAR, 'KeywordModel')
+        for value in ('if', 'IF', 'If', 'else', 'ELSE', 'Else'):
+            with self.assertRaises(FailedParse, msg=value):
+                model.parse(value)
+        self.assertEqual(['IF'], model.parse('IF', ignorecase=False))
+        self.assertEqual(['else'], model.parse('else', ignorecase=False))
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            model.parse('ELSE', ignorecase=False)
+
+    def test_generated_parser_matches_model_and_overrides(self):
+        namespace = {}
+        exec(codegen(tatsu.compile(KEYWORD_GRAMMAR, 'GeneratedCase')), namespace)
+        parser = namespace['GeneratedCaseParser']()
+        for value in ('if', 'IF', 'If', 'else', 'ELSE', 'Else'):
+            with self.assertRaises(FailedParse, msg=value):
+                parser.parse(value)
+        self.assertEqual(['IF'], parser.parse('IF', ignorecase=False))
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            parser.parse('IF')
+
+        literal = {}
+        exec(codegen(tatsu.compile(LITERAL_TRUE, 'GeneratedLiteral')), literal)
+        generated = literal['GeneratedLiteralParser']()
+        self.assertEqual('AbC', generated.parse('ABC'))
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            generated.parse('ABC', ignorecase=False)
+
+        strict = {}
+        exec(codegen(tatsu.compile(LITERAL_FALSE, 'GeneratedStrict')), strict)
+        strict_parser = strict['GeneratedStrictParser']()
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            strict_parser.parse('abc')
+        self.assertEqual('AbC', strict_parser.parse('abc', ignorecase=True))
+        with self.assertRaises(FailedParse):
+            strict_parser.parse('abc')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /testbed

# Use Node 20 (compatible with this older project using PhantomJS/Grunt)
dev-switch node 20

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Build the engine
mkdir -p build/dist
npx grunt ts:core
npx grunt concat

# Compile test specs
npx grunt ts:specs

# Run all Jasmine tests (includes SceneSpec.ts)
# OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null is required to work around PhantomJS + OpenSSL 3.x incompatibility
OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null npx grunt jasmine
